groups.label: Then
groups.hint: Quotes, tools and the mailer kit.

tasks.title: Link the business in RAM
tasks.summary: So either of you can lodge the BAS online. A Standard myID works if you link by phone.
body: Linking online needs a Strong myID, which needs an Australian passport. If you can't get Strong, RAM links you by phone with a Standard myID instead.
Alternative: if Dan has an Australian passport, he gets a Strong myID, links the business online himself, then authorises you.
steps: Check the name on your myID matches your name on the ABN record exactly. If not, raise it on the call.
Call 1300 287 539, option 3 then option 1, for a proof of identity check. Have the ABN and the myID app ready.
Once linked, log in to RAM and authorise Dan. He accepts with his own myID within 7 days.
Log in to Online services for business and check you can see the activity statement.

links.label: RAM: other ways to link your business
ATO: online services with myID and RAM

tasks.title: One lawyer quote
tasks.summary: One fixed fee to review the partnership agreement and the client order agreement.
body: Cheaper than two separate jobs. Or start from Arts Law templates.

tasks.title: Insurance quote
tasks.summary: Professional indemnity. Public liability can wait.
body: No site visits, so public liability is less urgent, but some clients will ask for it.

tasks.title: Put tools on the business
tasks.summary: Pay subscriptions from the business account. Log every receipt.
steps: Move Claude, Google Workspace, Porkbun, Framer (for client sites) and any paid fonts to the business card.
Send each receipt to Claude: it's renamed, filed in the asnew receipts folder and logged in the Expenses Sheet.
Anything either of you paid personally goes in the Sheet too, to be paid back.

tasks.title: Mailer kit and a test run
tasks.summary: Silhouette Cameo 5 for the press-out card. Printing at a local print shop, not an EcoTank.
body: A print shop handles heavy uncoated card and brand colours better than an EcoTank, with no upfront cost. Revisit a printer only if you're sending several a week.
steps: Buy the standard Cameo 5, not the Alpha, on the business card.
Find a print shop that does single sheets of heavy stock quickly, and ask them to print the Silhouette registration marks.
Give them the print-safe lime: CMYK 22/0/76/0.
Cut a test sheet of the real stock. 350gsm may need two passes.
Post a few to yourselves to check the ties hold through sorting.

tasks.title: asnew.com.au, and let asnew.studio go
tasks.summary: Register asnew.com.au and redirect it to asnew.au. Don't renew asnew.studio.
steps: Register asnew.com.au. It's open to you because it matches the business name.
Add it to Cloudflare and redirect it to asnew.au.
Turn off auto-renew on asnew.studio once nothing points at it.

tasks.title: Website basics
tasks.summary: Privacy policy, terms and the ABN in the footer. No cookie banner needed.
body: Under $3m turnover, asnew is exempt from the Privacy Act, and Australia has no cookie law. A short, plain privacy policy is still worth having, so nobody feels caught out.
Revisit the banner question if you add Google Analytics, an ad pixel or anything aimed at EU or UK visitors.
steps: Privacy policy: what you collect (enquiry emails, order details), why, and that you don't sell it.
Pitch pages: say you're notified when one is opened, with the rough location and device.
Cookies: none for visitors. One on your own devices, to skip your own visits.
Payments: handled by Stripe on its own pages; you never see card details.
Terms page, and the ABN in the footer.
Add the policy to the lawyer's review.

tasks.title: Launch the website
tasks.summary: The pages are designed and the prices are in. Build once these are settled.
steps: Pick the About footage frame it opens and rests on (launch homepage, About, phone About).
Email when someone sends an order (the task below), so SEND IT works.
Privacy and Terms: update after the lawyer's review, then add the date.
Then tell Claude to build: launch homepage, How it works, FAQ, About, Menu, Start, Sent, Privacy, Terms, 404, favicon and share images.

tasks.title: Short link for card payments
tasks.summary: Make asnew.au/pay go to the Stripe concept-fee link, then show that on invoices instead of the long Stripe address. Not urgent.
steps: Either: in Cloudflare, add a Redirect Rule sending asnew.au/pay to https://buy.stripe.com/bJeeVd5X7ciUfjR1iNfnO00.
Or: wait for the website build in December, and Claude adds it there.
Check asnew.au/pay opens the $2,750 checkout.
Tell Claude to switch concept-fee invoices to show asnew.au/pay.

tasks.title: Switch the contact email to studio@
tasks.summary: The registrations list Dan's personal Outlook. Change it to studio@asnew.au, and add the studio phone.
body: studio@asnew.au is working, so put it on every registration so ATO and ASIC mail comes to the business, not one person.
From then on, if a contact detail you've given stops being right, update it within 28 days.
steps: ABN, GST and TFN: update the email in Online services for business once RAM is linked, or on the ABR site.
Business name: update the holder's contact details in ASIC's online services.
Add the studio phone, 0485 674 325, to both while you're there.
Check both registers show the new email.

links.label: ASIC: change business name holder details

tasks.title: Record VCO's payment as asnew income
tasks.summary: It went into Martin's NZ account, but it's still asnew's money: it goes in the ledger, the BAS and the split.
body: VCO's invoice 001-1 is NZD 4,500, GST-free as an export. Cash basis, so it counts in the quarter the money lands.
steps: When it's paid, log it in the asnew ledger: the date it landed, the AUD amount received, GST-free.
Move the AUD amount into the NAB account, or note it as held by Martin for the quarterly split.
Add VCO's contact name and email to the job in the Jobs tracker.

tasks.title: Set NAB as the default account on invoices
tasks.summary: In the Jobs tracker's invoice settings, with the bank's full account name.
steps: New invoice → set who gets paid to the NAB account, using the full account name the bank shows.
Save it as the default.
Add “Our bank details never change by email” to the invoice note.

tasks.title: Email when a prospect opens their pitch
tasks.summary: An email to studio@ each time a pitch page (asnew.au/<name>) is opened. No other analytics.
body: A small function in asnew-site sends the email after someone has been on the page for about 5 seconds, which filters out bots and link previews. The email says which business, where they are, the device and whether they came from the mailer or an email.
Your own visits are skipped once you've opened /me on each of your devices.
steps: Make a free Resend account and add its DNS records for asnew.au in Cloudflare. They sit on a send. subdomain, so the Google email records stay as they are.
Put the Resend key in Cloudflare Pages as a secret, not in the repo.
Claude adds the function and the 5-second signal to the pitch pages.
Point mailer QR codes at ?src=mailer and email links at ?src=email.
Open /me on each of your phones and laptops.
Open a test pitch page from another phone and check the email arrives.

tasks.title: Email us when someone sends an order
tasks.summary: SEND IT on the Start page emails their order and answers to studio@, and sends them a copy. Uses the same Resend set-up as the pitch alerts.
body: A small function in asnew-site takes what they picked on the Menu (prices +GST) and their four answers, then emails them to studio@. Reply-to is their address, so you just hit Reply.
An invisible Cloudflare Turnstile check keeps bots out. Nothing is stored: the email is the record, and the job still goes in the Jobs tracker by hand.
steps: Do the Resend set-up from the pitch alerts task first.
Add a free Turnstile widget for the site in Cloudflare and put its secret key in Cloudflare Pages.
Claude designs their copy of the order in the asnew brand: what they picked, prices +GST, their answers, and "We'll have a look and email you."
Claude adds the function and connects SEND IT to it. One send emails studio@ and their copy at the same time.
Send a test order from your phone and check both emails, the Reply-to on each and the confirmation screen. Check their copy doesn't land in spam in Gmail and Outlook.

tasks.title: File the trade mark
tasks.summary: “asnew” and the new mark together, classes 35 and 42, in both your names.
body: Registering the business name doesn't mean you own it. Only a trade mark does that, and it matters if asnew carries the brand for years.
A partnership isn't a legal person, so the mark is filed in both your names. TM Headstart gives an early read on the risk that “asnew” is seen as descriptive.

tasks.title: Client terms
tasks.summary: Most is decided. Settle tweak rounds, then the lawyer's review.
steps: Rounds of tweaks: one at each check, or two.
Invoice terms: 7 days, as the tracker defaults to?
If a client goes quiet: how long the job stays paused.
Lawyer's review.
body: Decided: concept fee $2,500 +GST by card, the rest by bank transfer when final files are delivered; a new concept costs another concept fee; 14 days of free fixes after handover; websites in Framer only; the $500 referral bonus.

tasks.title: First BAS
tasks.summary: October to December 2026. Probably not nil: VCO's payment goes on it.
body: If VCO pays before 31 Dec, the BAS shows it as a GST-free export sale, so the nil-by-phone line can't be used. Lodge it in Online services for business once RAM is linked.
Registered for GST means a BAS every quarter, nil or not.
steps: Online services for business, once RAM is linked.
Nil BAS only: phone 13 72 26, any time.
Or a BAS agent, which also pushes the due date later.

links.label: ATO: lodging in Online services for business

tasks.title: Google Workspace trial ends
tasks.summary: Add billing on the business card before the 14-day trial ends, with a promo code if you have one.
body: A promo code only works for new customers and goes in at billing set-up. The discount won't show in the order summary.

tasks.title: Mailer to the parked prospects
tasks.summary: Once there are 2–3 case studies, a cheap mailer to the C-tier and parked prospects. No spec work: just a link to the website and its cases.
steps: Wait for 2–3 live case studies (VCO launches Jan or Feb).
Clean the list: drop anyone now using AI imagery or who has rebranded.
One template, with a case from their own sector on the front (accountants see an accountant).
A plain postcard, no press-out card.
Follow-up email two weeks later if they haven't replied.

tasks.title: Review prices
tasks.summary: Leave them for now. Look again once five jobs are done. Same time as Xero.

tasks.title: Tighten DMARC
tasks.summary: Once studio@ mail keeps passing, change the _dmarc record in Cloudflare DNS from p=none to p=quarantine.

tasks.title: First tax returns
tasks.summary: The partnership's return for the year to 30 June 2027, then your own.

tasks.title: Renew the business name
tasks.summary: ASIC emails a reminder. Renew before it lapses.

tasks.title: Partnership
tasks.summary: Both personally liable. Look at a Pty Ltd once the work grows.

tasks.title: ABN
tasks.summary: Registered 8 Nov 2026.

tasks.title: Business name ASNEW
tasks.summary: Registered for three years.

tasks.title: GST
tasks.summary: From 8 Nov 2026. Quarterly BAS, cash basis. It sits on the ABN: there's no separate number.

tasks.title: Partnership TFN
tasks.summary: Received. Keep it private: never on invoices or the site.

tasks.title: asnew.au and studio@asnew.au
tasks.summary: Domain at Porkbun, one Google Workspace mailbox. SPF, DKIM and DMARC all pass (23 Nov). Some mail may hit spam for a few weeks while the domain is new.

tasks.title: Website and pitch pages
tasks.summary: One GitHub repo, served by Cloudflare Pages on asnew.au.
body: Not GitHub Pages: its terms ban sites that take payments, and the pitch pages take concept fees.
Pitch pages sit at asnew.au/<name>, e.g. asnew.au/wte, as printed on the mailers. Each one gets a noindex header in _headers and stays out of the sitemap, so it can't be found by search.
steps: Make a private repo, asnew-site, under a business account or organisation. Add Dan.
Starter files: a holding homepage, pitch pages at asnew.au/<name>, and a _headers file that marks each one noindex. Claude writes these.
Make a Cloudflare account with a business email. Turn on two-factor sign-in.

Add asnew.au to Cloudflare on the free plan. Before you swap the nameservers at Porkbun for Cloudflare's, check every email record came across: MX, SPF, google._domainkey and _dmarc. Miss one and studio@ mail bounces or lands in spam.
Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git → asnew-site. No framework, no build command. Check the pages.dev link loads.
Once DNS has switched: Custom domains → add asnew.au and www.asnew.au. Redirect www.
Once the site is live, delete the wildcard *.asnew.au CNAME (Porkbun's parking page) if it came across.
Push a test pitch page to /test- plus a random ending. Check it loads, isn't linked anywhere and has the noindex header. Delete it.

tasks.title: Social handles
tasks.summary: Instagram and LinkedIn handles claimed, with studio@asnew.au as the login.

tasks.title: Open the bank account
tasks.summary: NAB Business Everyday, the $0 option. Payments and paying for tools wait on this.
body: It opens online for partnerships. Clients paying “asnew” into an account in a personal name get a name-mismatch warning from their bank, so this matters before the first invoice.
steps: Apply online with the ABN and the business name.
Both of you verify your ID.
Give both of you full access.
Add the BSB and account number to the invoice template.

tasks.title: Set up the books: a spreadsheet
tasks.summary: The asnew Expenses Sheet and the asnew receipts folder in Drive. No Xero for now.
body: The ATO doesn't require accounting software. Records must be kept for five years, in English, and explain every transaction.
Keep a tax invoice for any purchase over $82.50 including GST, or you can't claim that GST back.
Look at Xero again after five jobs, when you review prices. Its bank feed is the main thing it would save you.
steps: Make the ledger: date, who, what, category, ex GST, GST, total, money in or out, receipt link. Claude can set it up.
Make a shared receipts folder. One file per receipt, named date-supplier-amount.
Log everything at least monthly, from the business account.

links.label: ATO: when you can claim a GST credit

tasks.title: Clear the name and the new mark
tasks.summary: Trade mark search for asnew and the new block mark. Before the mailers go to print.
steps: Search “asnew”, “as new” and “anew” in classes 35 and 42.
Run the new block mark (filleted A and N) through the image search.
Note anything close and send it to Claude for a read.

links.label: IP Australia: search existing trade marks

tasks.title: Get a business phone number
tasks.summary: For the bank, the ATO, suppliers and clients once they've signed. Not on the website.
body: Prospects still come in by website and email. The number is for accounts, verification codes and client calls once a job has started.
steps: Pick one: a prepaid eSIM on one of your phones, or a cheap prepaid SIM in a spare phone.
Decide who carries it, or forward it to both of you.
Use it for the bank account, the ABR and ASIC records, and the business accounts.
Add it to the email signature and the order email, not the website.

tasks.title: Tax invoice template
tasks.summary: In the asnew brand. Claude can make it.
steps: Say “Tax invoice”, and show the ABN, date, what was sold and the GST.
From $1,000, add the client's name or ABN.
Add the bank details once the account is open.

tasks.title: Partnership agreement
tasks.summary: Write down what you've already agreed.
steps: 50/50 profit, paid quarterly.
$1,000 limit on spending alone.
Either of you can sign client agreements.
The name, the mark and the work belong to the business.
The rule that keeps Dan's day job clear.
What happens if one of you leaves. A change of partners can mean a new ABN and TFN.

tasks.title: One accountant call (optional)
tasks.summary: How much to set aside for tax, and a check of the spreadsheet set-up.
body: The partnership pays no income tax itself. Each of you pays tax on your half, so set part of each payout aside. The ATO may put you on PAYG instalments after the first return.

tasks.title: Card payments
tasks.summary: Card for the concept fee only, through Stripe. The rest is bank transfer.
body: Card surcharges are banned from 1 Oct 2026, so the Stripe fee is absorbed. That's why card stops at the concept fee.
